question: In recent days, worrying information has emerged in the Czech Republic about spoiled meat possibly being served in KFC fast food establishments operated by AmRest. This information indicates a potential threat to consumer health that may affect not only the Czech Republic, but also other Member States where this chain operates. Given the seriousness of these allegations, which affect both public health and consumer confidence in the European food safety system, I would like to ask the following questions: 1.
What steps does the Commission intend to take to investigate this case promptly and ensure that the products sold in KFC/AmRest establishments comply with EU food safety standards?

Does the Commission plan to call on the national supervisory authorities of all Member States to carry out thorough and coordinated inspections of the establishments from the KFC chain and similar establishments throughout the EU?

Is the Commission considering taking measures to tighten up the monitoring and traceability of meat and other food products within the single market, with a view to preventing such threats to public health from arising in the future?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (11.11.2025) It is not the Commission’s role to investigate individual cases of possible non-compliance on food safety requirements. It is for the national authority where the food establishment is located to carry out such investigation. Accordingly, the Czech Authorities informed the Commission on their investigations and corrective actions taken.

The Commission has requested the Czech authorities to distribute their findings to other Member States through the Commission’s Administrative Assistance and Cooperation Network in order to alert them on these infringements that may occur also on their territory. The Commission considers that current food hygiene and traceability rules provide sufficient guarantees to prevent related threats to public health.
The enforcement of existing rules by the competent authorities of the Member States seems more relevant than imposing additional requirements.
